choices.why: This white track-arm sofa is slim and not too deep, so it suits the narrow room, and its birch legs echo the light oak floor.
The long, light-legged white console blends into the white right wall and gives the TV ample, uncluttered storage without weighing down the narrow space.
No round table was offered, so this compact solid birch table is the closest fit; its warm light wood matches the floor and the sofa legs, and it suits a two-person dining spot by the balcony.
These birch chairs belong to the same family as the table, so the two of them make a cohesive Scandinavian dining corner.
The round black coffee table picks up the black balcony frame and adds contrast against the white sofa and walls, and its rounded edges help circulation in the narrow room.
At 160 cm wide, this dark grey flatweave rug fits the room's width and anchors the seating area against the light floor.
This black dome pendant replaces the bare bulb with character, and it ties in with the coffee table and the black window frame.
The slim drum-shade floor lamp gives soft reading and TV light next to the sofa without taking up floor space.
These sheer white linen curtains soften the balcony door while keeping the room bright.
Beige linen cushions add warmth to the white sofa and connect with the wood tones in the room.
The tall braided money tree is the largest plant on offer, and it brings height and greenery to the bright corner by the balcony.
The black-and-white photo prints match the room's white and black palette and fill the long wall above the sofa well.

answer.why: A light Scandinavian base of white and birch matches the white walls and oak floor, while black accents in the coffee table, pendant, rug and photos echo the balcony frame for a cohesive, airy look. The narrow, compact pieces leave room to move through this long room.
